page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C core with 2 threads, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a large 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for matrix math and vector operations. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio, and includes 118 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core performance but limited multi-core scaling due to the dual-thread single-core physical layout. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated as average at 2215.58, while the multi-core score of 2263.98 is relatively weak. Memory performance shows a similar trend, with an average PassMark memory score of 1927.71, but weak uncached read and write bandwidths of 22.92 GB/sec and 12.15 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and Redis SET performance also fall into the weaker tier, with Redis achieving 4.01 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning workloads, the instance achieves an average text generation speed of 88.94 tokens per second on a small 135M LLM model, though prompt processing speeds remain low.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2ds_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated compute resources at a lower entry point than larger instances in the same family, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. However, the primary tradeoff is the single physical core bottleneck, which restricts multi-threaded throughput and heavy computational scaling. This instance is best suited for small-scale databases, caching layers, lightweight web serving, and memory-intensive development or testing environments where a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio is required without high CPU core counts.
